chapters.title: Case Endings and Dative Subjects
chapters.label: ch:ka-dative-case
chapters.canDo: I can say that I know Kannada the way Kannada itself says it — with no subject at all, marking myself with the dative -ge.

payoff.summary: Say ನನಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಗೊತ್ತು — "to-me Kannada known" — set against ನಾನು ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾತನಾಡುತ್ತೇನೆ, then line up the four Dravidian datives -ge · -ukku · -ku · -ikku.

chapters.title: Numbers One to Ten
chapters.label: ch:ka-numbers-one-to-ten
chapters.canDo: I can count from one to ten in Kannada and read the Kannada digits ೧–೧೦ off the page.

payoff.summary: Count ಒಂದು through ಹತ್ತು aloud, read the digits ೬ ೭ ೮ ೯ ೧೦, and hear the p → h shift that turns Tamil pattu into Kannada hattu.

chapters.title: Please
chapters.label: ch:ka-please
chapters.canDo: I can say please in Kannada, and use the polite verb ending Kannada reaches for far more often than the word itself.

payoff.summary: Build ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು out of daya ("compassion") + iṭṭu ("having placed"), then make the everyday polite request instead: ಕುಳಿತುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, "please sit."

chapters.title: Sorry
chapters.label: ch:ka-sorry
chapters.canDo: I can apologise in Kannada and ask someone to forgive me.

payoff.summary: Say ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ, trace it back through kṣamisu to Sanskrit kṣamā, and contrast it with Tamil's unrelated maṉṉikkavum.

chapters.title: Days of the Week
chapters.label: ch:ka-days-of-the-week
chapters.canDo: I can name any day of the week in Kannada, including the Sunday that uses a different sun-name from Hindi's.

payoff.summary: Run Somavāra through Śanivāra, then name Sunday ಭಾನುವಾರ and say why it is Bhānu here where Hindi says Ravi.

chapters.title: Four Core Colours
chapters.label: ch:ka-core-colours
chapters.canDo: I can name four basic colours in Kannada — black, white, red, and blue.

payoff.summary: Say ಕಪ್ಪು, ಬಿಳಿ, ಕೆಂಪು — the three native colours — then the borrowed ನೀಲಿ, and point out that the week is Sanskritic where the colours are not.

chapters.title: Family
chapters.label: ch:ka-family
chapters.canDo: I can name my parents and my brothers and sisters in Kannada, choosing the right word for older or younger.

payoff.summary: Name ಅಪ್ಪ and ಅಮ್ಮ, then the four age-graded siblings ಅಣ್ಣ · ತಮ್ಮ · ಅಕ್ಕ · ತಂಗಿ, where age is chosen before gender.

chapters.title: Head and Hand
chapters.label: ch:ka-head-and-hand
chapters.canDo: I can name the head and the hand in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Say ತಲೆ and ಕೈ, and hear how nearly unchanged they are across Tamil, Malayalam and Kannada.

chapters.title: Seasons
chapters.label: ch:ka-seasons
chapters.canDo: I can name the four seasons in Kannada, including the monsoon that actually shapes the Karnataka year.

payoff.summary: Say ಬೇಸಿಗೆ, ಮಳೆಗಾಲ and ಚಳಿಗಾಲ from native roots, then the doubly-Sanskrit ವಸಂತ ಋತು for spring.

chapters.title: Water and Rice
chapters.label: ch:ka-water-and-rice
chapters.canDo: I can ask for water in Kannada and tell raw rice apart from cooked rice.

payoff.summary: Say ನೀರು — matching Tamil's neer, not Malayalam's — then separate ಅಕ್ಕಿ, raw rice, from ಅನ್ನ, the cooked rice on the plate.

chapters.title: The Traditional Months
chapters.label: ch:ka-traditional-months
chapters.canDo: I can name the twelve traditional Kannada months and say when the new year Ugadi falls.

payoff.summary: Recite Caitra through Phālguṇa, place Ugadi at Chaitra Śukla Pratipada, and note that this calendar is shared with Hindi, not with Tamil or Malayalam.

chapters.title: Noon and Midnight
chapters.label: ch:ka-noon-and-midnight
chapters.canDo: I can say noon and midnight in Kannada and point out the "middle" word they share.

payoff.summary: Say ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ and ಮಧ್ಯರಾತ್ರಿ, then isolate the madhya sitting inside both.

chapters.title: Telling Time
chapters.label: ch:ka-telling-time
chapters.canDo: I can tell someone the time on the hour in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Say ಗಂಟೆ — hour, and also "bell" — then ಒಂದು ಗಂಟೆ and ಎರಡು ಗಂಟೆ for one and two o'clock.

chapters.title: Asking Someone's Age
chapters.label: ch:ka-asking-age
chapters.canDo: I can ask someone how old they are in Kannada and give my own age in return.

payoff.summary: Ask ನಿನ್ನ ವಯಸ್ಸು ಎಷ್ಟು? and answer ನನ್ನ ವಯಸ್ಸು ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು — a complete verbless exchange about age.

chapters.title: Numbers 11–20 and Weather
chapters.label: ch:ka-numbers-and-weather
chapters.canDo: I can say what the weather is doing in Kannada and count past ten up to twenty.

payoff.summary: Say ಹವಾಮಾನ — the Persian hava plus Sanskrit māna — and report the weather with ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತಿದೆ, "rain is coming."

chapters.title: Dog and Cat
chapters.label: ch:ka-dog-and-cat
chapters.canDo: I can name a dog and a cat in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Say ನಾಯಿ, an unambiguously native Dravidian root, and ಬೆಕ್ಕು, a different ancient root from Tamil's everyday cat word.

chapters.title: Green and Yellow
chapters.label: ch:ka-green-and-yellow
chapters.canDo: I can name green and yellow in Kannada, on top of the four colours I already had.

payoff.summary: Say ಹಸಿರು, a true cousin of Tamil paccai and Telugu pacca, then ಹಳದಿ, the turmeric-borrowing that is secretly a cousin of German gelb.

chapters.title: Day
chapters.label: ch:ka-day
chapters.canDo: I can say "day" in Kannada and tell it apart from the native word for daytime.

payoff.summary: Say ದಿನ, kept whole as a Sanskrit tatsama where Hindi's din eroded, and set it against native ಹಗಲು, which means daytime rather than a day.

chapters.title: Night
chapters.label: ch:ka-night
chapters.canDo: I can say "night" in Kannada and recognise it inside the midnight word I already knew.

payoff.summary: Say ರಾತ್ರಿ, find it again inside ಮಧ್ಯರಾತ್ರಿ, and note that native ಇರುಳು lost its job where ಹಗಲು kept a different one.

chapters.title: Good Night
chapters.label: ch:ka-good-night
chapters.canDo: I can wish someone good night in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Say ಶುಭ ರಾತ್ರಿ — "auspicious night" — pairing the ರಾತ್ರಿ already learned with śubha, from a root meaning "to be beautiful."

chapters.title: Morning
chapters.label: ch:ka-morning
chapters.canDo: I can say "morning" in Kannada using the language's own native word for it.

payoff.summary: Say ಬೆಳಗ್ಗೆ, trace it to beḷagu ("to dawn") and beḷaku ("light"), and contrast it with the Sanskrit dina, rātri and madhyāhna around it.

chapters.title: Evening
chapters.label: ch:ka-evening
chapters.canDo: I can say "evening" in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Say ಸಂಜೆ, follow it back through Maharashtri Prakrit to Sanskrit saṃdhyā, and set it beside Hindi's साँझ, the same root down a different Prakrit road.

chapters.title: Afternoon
chapters.label: ch:ka-afternoon
chapters.canDo: I can say "afternoon" in Kannada and keep it distinct from noon.

payoff.summary: Say ಅಪರಾಹ್ನ, split it into apara ("latter") + ahna ("day"), and match that -ahna against the one in ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ.

chapters.title: Good Morning
chapters.label: ch:ka-good-morning
chapters.canDo: I can wish someone good morning in Kannada and judge when it will sound too formal.

payoff.summary: Say ಶುಭೋದಯ — śubha + udaya, "auspicious rising" — and note the formal/written skew that makes ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ the safer casual morning greeting.

chapters.title: Good Evening
chapters.label: ch:ka-good-evening
chapters.canDo: I can wish someone good evening in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Say ಶುಭ ಸಂಜೆ, correct the common claim that ಸಂಜೆ is native Dravidian, and keep ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ as the all-hours fallback.

chapters.title: Good Afternoon
chapters.label: ch:ka-good-afternoon
chapters.canDo: I can wish someone good afternoon in Kannada, and fall back on ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ when I want a greeting that fits any hour.

payoff.summary: Say ಶುಭ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ — built on the "noon" word rather than ಅಪರಾಹ್ನ — and reach instead for ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, the greeting confirmed to work at any time of day.

chapters.title: The Core Verbs
chapters.label: ch:ka-core-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can build a Kannada verb as stem plus tense plus person, swap the middle bead for the past, hear the p → h law that separates Kannada from its three sisters, and say why ಗೊತ್ತು carries no person at all.

payoff.summary: Say ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು, name the three slots that built iruttēne, hōguttēne and nōḍuttēne, explain which slot ಗೊತ್ತು leaves empty and where its person went instead, and give the sound-law behind pōgu → hōgu.

chapters.title: Four Verbs of Mind and Page
chapters.label: ch:ka-mind-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can say I think, I understand, I read and I write in Kannada, name the suffix that turns a Sanskrit noun into a Kannada verb, use the ending that hands an action back to its doer, and give both of the front-of-the-word sound laws that separate Kannada from Tamil.

payoff.summary: Say ನಾನು ಕನ್ನಡ ಬರೆಯುತ್ತೇನೆ, keep it apart from ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ one vowel away, explain the glide a vowel-final stem needs, take bare back to the Dravidian line-drawing root behind Tamil வரை, set the v → b law beside the p → h law, and count this chapter’s four verbs onto Chapter 32’s six to reach hattu.

chapters.title: Four Verbs Between People
chapters.label: ch:ka-social-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can say I take, I ask and I help in Kannada, say I like Kannada in a sentence with no verb in it, place it beside the two other dative sentences I have built, and show that the frame it uses was Kannada’s own before any Sanskrit word moved into it.

payoff.summary: Say ನನಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಇಷ್ಟ and unpack it as “to me, Kannada, a liking” with no verb at all; line it up against ನನಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತು and ನನಗೆ ಬೇಕು; show that the inherited bēku takes the same dative and answers Tamil vēṇṭum by the v → b law; and trace iṣṭa to the Indo-European root behind English ask, unrelated to the kēḷu of the same chapter.

chapters.title: Family and Friends
chapters.label: ch:ka-family-and-friends
chapters.canDo: I can name my family as a group in Kannada and name a friend, and say which of the two words is native and which is a Sanskrit loan.

payoff.summary: Say ಇದು ನನ್ನ ಕುಟುಂಬ and ಇವನು ನನ್ನ ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ, trace kuṭumba and snēhita back to Sanskrit, and set snēhita beside the native pair ಗೆಳೆಯ/ಗೆಳತಿ.

chapters.title: One Root, Three Endings
chapters.label: ch:ka-child-son-daughter
chapters.canDo: I can say child, son and daughter in Kannada, and show how one shared root with three different endings does the job Chapter 12 needed four separate words for.

payoff.summary: Line up ಮಗು, ಮಗ and ಮಗಳು against Proto-Dravidian *maka, and contrast gender-by-ending here with Chapter 12's four unrelated age-graded sibling words.

chapters.title: Four Words on the Face
chapters.label: ch:ka-face-words
chapters.canDo: I can name my eye, ear, nose and mouth in Kannada, and say which of the four the Dravidian family agrees on closely and which one splits.

payoff.summary: Name ಕಣ್ಣು, ಕಿವಿ, ಮೂಗು and ಬಾಯಿ, and finally explain ಬಾಯಿ — the word this book already used twice, unglossed, as proof of the v → b law behind ಬಾ and ಬರೆ.

chapters.title: The Heart
chapters.label: ch:ka-heart
chapters.canDo: I can name my heart in Kannada and say why it is a genuine Indo-European cousin of the English word, not just a resemblance.

payoff.summary: Say ನನ್ನ ಹೃದಯ, read the vocalic-r sign ೃ against Chapter 14's independent ಋ, and trace hṛdaya to the same Proto-Indo-European root as English heart, Latin cor and Greek kardía.

chapters.title: Tea, Coffee, Milk
chapters.label: ch:ka-tea-coffee-milk
chapters.canDo: I can politely ask for tea, coffee or milk in Kannada, and trace each word along the road it travelled to get here.

payoff.summary: Ask ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು ಚಹಾ, ಕಾಫಿ or ಹಾಲು, follow chā through Persian and kāphi through five languages, then explain hālu — the word Chapter 32 already recited unglossed as proof of the p → h law.

chapters.title: A Meal
chapters.label: ch:ka-a-meal
chapters.canDo: I can say I am having a meal in Kannada, using the word Chapter 32 used once and never explained, and place it at the hour of two greetings I already know.

payoff.summary: Say ಊಟ ಮಾಡು, explain ūṭa against everyday tinnu, read the independent vowel ಊ, and place the word at the hour of ಶುಭ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ and before ಶುಭ ರಾತ್ರಿ.

chapters.title: Pointing, and Asking
chapters.label: ch:kn-pointing-and-asking
chapters.canDo: I can point at something in Kannada and ask who or where it is — and I can say what the six words have in common.

payoff.summary: Say the near word, the far word and the question word in a row, and name the part that changed.

chapters.title: Describing Things
chapters.label: ch:kn-describing-things
chapters.canDo: I can point at something in Kannada and ask who or where it is — and I can say what the six words have in common.

payoff.summary: Say the near word, the far word and the question word in a row, and name the part that changed.

chapters.title: More Everyday Verbs
chapters.label: ch:ka-more-verbs
chapters.canDo: I can tell someone to come, sit, stand and give in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Complete KA-C43-give and say all four verbs in order.

chapters.title: Verbs of Seeing and Saying
chapters.label: ch:ka-see-say
chapters.canDo: I can tell someone to look, listen, speak and write in Kannada.

payoff.summary: Complete KA-C44-write and say all four verbs in order.

chapters.title: The Older Generation
chapters.label: ch:ka-older-generation
chapters.canDo: I can name four more family and people words in this language.

payoff.summary: Complete KA-C45-wife and say all four words in order.
